responsibilities: Invite customers to ask about available items.
Explain prices and requested quantities clearly.
Respond politely to requests for a lower price.
Clarify the amount or measure supplied.
Confirm payment, change and the transaction outcome.
Recognise returning customers and invite them back respectfully.

jobKnowledge.title: Selling unit
jobKnowledge.text: The price may apply to an individual item, a group or a measured amount. The vendor's English should make that unit clear so the customer understands what the stated price covers.

jobKnowledge.title: Price flexibility
jobKnowledge.text: An available selling price and a customer's proposed price are different pieces of information. The vendor can explain an offer or decline it without inventing a discount or implying that bargaining is always available.

jobKnowledge.title: Transaction details
jobKnowledge.text: An exchange may involve cash, UPI or another available method. Communication distinguishes the amount due, the payment result and any change. It does not prescribe payment-system procedures.

jobKnowledge.title: Returning customers
jobKnowledge.text: A returning customer may refer to an earlier purchase. The vendor can clarify the current request without assuming that today's stock, amount or price is unchanged.

responsibilities: Name the requested vegetable or clarify which variety is wanted.
Explain differences between available sizes or varieties using observable descriptions.
Clarify whether the customer wants a piece count or a measured weight.
Offer an available substitute when the requested vegetable or quantity is unavailable.
Confirm mixed-item selections before calculating their separate amounts.

jobKnowledge.title: Produce identification
jobKnowledge.text: Customers may use different names for the same vegetable or ask for a particular variety. The seller can clarify by pointing to or describing the available produce without claiming that unfamiliar names are interchangeable.

jobKnowledge.title: Count and weight
jobKnowledge.text: A request for two pieces is different from a request for two kilos. The seller's language should confirm the vegetable and requested unit together, especially when an order contains several items.

jobKnowledge.title: Observable condition
jobKnowledge.text: Size, colour and visible condition can be described directly. Avoid unsupported claims about health benefits, chemical treatment or quality certification.

jobKnowledge.title: Substitutions
jobKnowledge.text: When the requested item is unavailable, the seller can describe an available alternative and ask whether the customer wants it. A substitution remains a customer choice.

responsibilities: Welcome the customer and discover their needs.
Describe relevant options and recommend a suitable choice.
Explain the stated price and what is included.
Respond to questions or objections using available information.
Discuss terms only within the worker's authority.
Confirm the customer's decision and agreed next step.
Follow up on an enquiry or quotation respectfully.
Acknowledge complaints and involve an appropriate colleague when needed.

jobKnowledge.title: Customer requirements
jobKnowledge.text: A recommendation is stronger when it follows the customer's stated purpose, preferences and constraints. Questions gather that information before the worker describes an option.

jobKnowledge.title: Quoted information
jobKnowledge.text: A quoted price and the final amount may differ when the customer changes the option or adds something. Explain what the current quotation covers rather than treating every amount as final.

jobKnowledge.title: Authority limits
jobKnowledge.text: A sales worker may need confirmation from a colleague before agreeing a request. English can clearly distinguish a confirmed offer from a proposal awaiting a decision.

jobKnowledge.title: Follow-up purpose
jobKnowledge.text: A useful follow-up refers to a previous enquiry and asks what the customer needs next. It does not assume that silence means agreement or that a purchase decision has been made.

jobKnowledge.title: Concern versus complaint
jobKnowledge.text: A concern before purchase may require an explanation or comparison. A complaint about an earlier exchange may require fact-checking and support from another team.

responsibilities: Clarify the customer's preferred vehicle model or version.
Compare relevant vehicle features from the available product information.
Explain what the selected vehicle quotation includes and what remains to be confirmed.
Arrange the customer's test-drive appointment and confirm the meeting details.
Ask permission before proceeding with an appointment-related action.
Follow up on a showroom visit or vehicle quotation with the customer's current questions.

jobKnowledge.title: Model and version
jobKnowledge.text: A model may be offered in more than one version. Features discussed with the customer should correspond to the actual option under consideration, using the dealership's available information.

jobKnowledge.title: Vehicle quotation
jobKnowledge.text: A vehicle quotation may show several components or optional additions. Explain only the information provided in the quotation and identify amounts awaiting confirmation, without offering finance or regulatory advice.

jobKnowledge.title: Appointment coordination
jobKnowledge.text: The pilot's test-drive communication covers the preferred option, availability, timing, meeting details and related customer questions. It does not cover vehicle operation or safety training.

jobKnowledge.title: Customer choice
jobKnowledge.text: A customer may compare options, request more information or postpone a decision. The worker can clarify that preference and agree on the next contact without claiming that an appointment commits the customer to buy.

responsibilities: Confirm pickup and order details with restaurant staff.
Contact the customer to clarify an address or meeting point.
Announce arrival and explain the purpose of the contact.
Communicate known delays and distinguish estimates from confirmed updates.
Acknowledge reports of wrong or missing items and clarify the discrepancy.
Pass issues outside the worker's authority to the support team.
Confirm the handover information needed for the current order.

jobKnowledge.title: Order identity
jobKnowledge.text: A delivery conversation needs enough order information to identify the relevant exchange. Clarify the available order details instead of assuming that every customer query concerns the same order.

jobKnowledge.title: Location clarification
jobKnowledge.text: A building name, flat number, entrance or landmark may need confirmation. The language task is to check those details with the customer or relevant contact, not to give route or driving guidance.

jobKnowledge.title: Delay updates
jobKnowledge.text: The worker can report the current known status and explain when an arrival time is uncertain. An estimate should not be described as a guaranteed time.

jobKnowledge.title: Discrepancy handling
jobKnowledge.text: A customer's report of a missing or wrong item needs clarification. The worker can communicate the reported discrepancy to the restaurant or support team without deciding an unauthorised refund or replacement.

jobKnowledge.title: Handover confirmation
jobKnowledge.text: The information requested to confirm a handover depends on the current order and workplace arrangement. The lesson may use supplied details but must not invent a universal platform procedure.

responsibilities: Clarify recruitment needs with the relevant department head.
Ask candidates for relevant experience and specific work examples.
Discuss role expectations and onboarding questions using confirmed workplace information.
Respond to employee queries and clarify information that is uncertain.
Discuss performance gaps with evidence and invite the employee's explanation.
Hear employee concerns respectfully and identify an appropriate next conversation.
Explain agreed workplace decisions or policies without adding unconfirmed rules.
Summarise actions, ownership and review points.

jobKnowledge.title: Recruitment conversation
jobKnowledge.text: An HR conversation gathers information about the role and the candidate's relevant experience. The examples and work constraints come from the industry context; the shared role core does not assume one sector.

jobKnowledge.title: Performance evidence
jobKnowledge.text: A performance gap is a difference between an agreed expectation and observed work. The manager's English should distinguish that evidence from assumptions about the employee's attitude or personal circumstances.

jobKnowledge.title: Employee concerns
jobKnowledge.text: An employee may need information, support or a further conversation. The manager can listen, clarify the concern and explain a known next contact without promising confidentiality or an outcome beyond their authority.

jobKnowledge.title: Policy communication
jobKnowledge.text: Explain only confirmed workplace information supplied in the situation. Do not invent employment rules, legal entitlements or disciplinary procedures.

jobKnowledge.title: Agreed follow-up
jobKnowledge.text: A clear summary identifies the actions discussed, the people responsible and any agreed review point. It does not imply that a conversation alone settles a recruitment decision or employee concern.
